ROOT_CAUSE.summary: A re-crawl can never produce meetEvent pages, because the event-results pass derives its event refs ONLY from swims pages fetched during that run, and resume skips swims pages that are already stored.
evidence: extensions/swimcloud-companion/src/crawler-content.ts, inside the page-1 fetch loop: `if (parsed.ok) swimsEventRefs.push(eventRefsOf(parsed.data));` -- refs come only from freshly-fetched pages.
runEventResultsPass is then called with `swimsPages: swimsEventRefs` (line ~1021) and plans from that alone: `planEventResultsSteps(input.meetId, input.swimsPages)`.

The code already warns about it at line ~1195: '<N> swims page(s) were skipped as already captured, so any event only they referenced is not fetched this run. Those swims import with their round unresolved, never with a guessed one.'
The stored capture has all 42 meetTeamSwims pages, so on a re-crawl resume skips ALL of them, swimsEventRefs is empty, and zero meetEvent pages are planned.
ROOT_CAUSE.whyItLooksLikeNothingHappened: The crawl completes normally and reports success. It simply had nothing new to fetch, so the capture store is untouched -- which is exactly what was observed.
ROOT_CAUSE.consequence: Round resolution is not broken; it is starved. The bridge resolves rounds correctly against a real event page (50/50 tests pass, including the Avery Henke and Oskar Cebula cases). It has never been given one for this meet.

fixDirection: Derive event refs from the STORED swims pages as well as freshly-fetched ones. The bytes are already on disk -- 42 meetTeamSwims pages in the capture store -- so no extra fetching is needed to learn the refs; only the meetEvent pages themselves get fetched. Candidate: have the crawler ask the app for the stored capture's event refs (the /parse route already parses stored pages server-side), union them with the refs gathered this run, and plan from the union.
